from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "A rabbit hops toward a carrot.",
            "The rabbit approaches infinitely close.",
            "It never becomes the carrot.",
            "This trend is the limit.",
            "We focus on the destination."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach", lecture_lines)
        
        rabbit = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        rabbit_label = Text("Rabbit", font_size=18, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(rabbit, UP)
        carrot = Star(n=5, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.3)
        limit_label = Text("Limit", font_size=18, color="#FF00FF").next_to(carrot, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(rabbit), FadeIn(rabbit_label), FadeIn(carrot), FadeIn(limit_label))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(rabbit, rabbit_label), "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(carrot, "E6")
        self.place_at_grid(limit_label, "D6")
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        curr_x = self.grid["E1"][0]
        target_x = self.grid["E6"][0]
        # Animation: Move half distance
        self.play(rabbit.animate.move_to([curr_x + (target_x - curr_x) / 2, self.grid["E1"][1], 0]),
                  rabbit_label.animate.move_to([curr_x + (target_x - curr_x) / 2, self.grid["E1"][1] + 0.3, 0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Animation: Move half of remaining
        new_x = rabbit.get_x()
        self.play(rabbit.animate.move_to([new_x + (target_x - new_x) / 2, self.grid["E1"][1], 0]),
                  rabbit_label.animate.move_to([new_x + (target_x - new_x) / 2, self.grid["E1"][1] + 0.3, 0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        flash = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FFFF00").move_to(carrot.get_center())
        self.play(ShowPassingFlash(flash))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Define epsilon for target accuracy.",
            "Define delta for input range.",
            "Does delta force epsilon bounds?",
            "The box trap proves it.",
            "Precision ensures the function limit."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Formal Rigor: Epsilon-Delta Definition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define axes and function
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 4], y_range=[-1, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6")
        self.add(axes)
        
        func = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 1)**2 + 1, color="#00FFFF")
        self.add(func)
        
        # Epsilon-Delta elements (to be updated later)
        epsilon_val = 0.5
        delta_val = 0.6
        c = 1.0
        L = 1.0
        
        # Epsilon rectangle
        epsilon_rect = Rectangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=2)
        epsilon_rect.set_width(3.0)
        epsilon_rect.set_height(epsilon_val * 2)
        epsilon_rect.move_to(axes.c2p(c, L))
        
        # Delta interval
        delta_line = Line(axes.c2p(c - delta_val, -0.1), axes.c2p(c + delta_val, -0.1), color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Labels
        eps_label = Text("Epsilon", font_size=18, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eps_label, "A2")
        del_label = Text("Delta", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(del_label, "F2")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(epsilon_rect))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(delta_line))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Shrink demonstration
        self.play(
            epsilon_rect.animate.set_height(0.4),
            delta_line.animate.set_length(0.4)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Computational Shortcut: L'Hôpital's Rule", ["Complex fractions defy simple limits.", "L'Hôpital compares growth rates.", "Use derivatives to compare speeds."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        frac = MathTex(r"\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(frac, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(frac))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        derivs = MathTex(r"f'(x), \quad g'(x)", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(derivs, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(derivs))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        new_frac = MathTex(r"\frac{f'(x)}{g'(x)}", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(new_frac, 'D5', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=frac.get_bottom(), end=new_frac.get_top(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(frac.copy(), new_frac))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

        # Create summary board elements
        concept_1 = Text("1. Intuition (Trends)", font_size=24, color=BLUE)

outline.topic: Mastering Limits: From Intuition to Precision and Shortcuts

sections.title: The Intuitive Foundation: The 'Zeno's Rabbit' Approach
sections.content: Introduce the limit as a 'trend' rather than a destination. Use a rabbit hopping toward a carrot; the rabbit gets infinitely close to the carrot (the limit) but never 'becomes' the carrot. Define the limit as the value a function approaches as x approaches a point c.
sections.example: A rabbit jumping toward a fence at x=2. Even if the ground at x=2 is missing (a hole), the rabbit knows exactly where it's headed.

sections.title: The Formal Rigor: Epsilon-Delta Definition (The Bodyguard Logic)
sections.content: Transition to formal definitions. Explain the 'Epsilon-Delta' game: If you want to get within a tiny distance (epsilon) of the target value L, can I find a distance (delta) around c that forces the function to stay within your goal? Visually, represent this as a shrinking box trap.
sections.example: A bodyguard (delta) ensures a celebrity (the function value) stays within a specific crowd fence (epsilon) as they walk toward the stage (x=c).

sections.title: The Computational Shortcut: L'Hôpital's Rule
sections.content: Introduce L'Hôpital's Rule for indeterminate forms (0/0). Explain that when a function is too complex to 'see' the limit, we compare their 'growth speeds' (derivatives) instead. Emphasize that this is like looking at the slopes of two competing racecars at the starting line.
sections.example: Comparing a fast-accelerating rocket (f(x)) and a slow-rising elevator (g(x)) as they both approach an 'indeterminate' starting gate at x=0.

sections.title: Synthesis & Visual Summary
sections.content: Briefly recap the journey: We moved from the rabbit's intuition (Concept), to the bodyguard's precision (Definition), to the rocket's acceleration (L'Hôpital). Provide a final visual flow chart showing when to use which tool.
sections.example: A 'Limit Toolbox' graphic: Use the Epsilon-Delta trap for proofs, and L'Hôpital's rocket fuel for quick calculation of complex fractions.
